newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CABINET AGREES BAILOUT FOR AERO.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CABINET AGREES BAILOUT FOR AERO.

text.p: Czech state institutions will combine in a 3.26 billion crown bailout for the troubled small aircraft maker Aero Vodochody a.s., while a tender is held to find a strategic partner, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Wednesday.
Klaus said the cabinet had assigned Minister of Industry and Trade Vladimir Dlouhy to submit criteria for the choice of a strategic partner.

The new partner would take a stake by raising the basic equity of Aero, a light military and civilian aircraft maker primarily owned by state-controlled institutions. Klaus did not detail what the size of the stake might be.
"The government feels it is in the interest of the state, for strategic and economic reasons, to preserve this enterprise," Klaus told reporters after a cabinet meeting.

"The end of the process should be when the state and its organs like the National Property Fund (FNM), and Konsolidacni Banka really got out of the problems (of Aero)... therefore we are interested in a private investor entering..." he said.
Klaus said he believed that the winner of a tender for a stake in Aero would be known by Christmas.

He said that the state-run Konsolidacni Banka would grant Aero a 2.3 billion crown loan while the National Property Fund would lend it 960 million crowns in a scheme which Klaus called a complicated mixture of debt payments and credit swaps.
Aero's flagship product is the L-159 light fighter aircraft, a version of its "Albatros" trainer plane being upgraded with Rockwell International Corp. avionics.

Klaus said the new partner would be able to take more shares in Aero -- most of which is held by the state-controlled Aero Holding a.s. and Konsolidacni Banka -- if it leads a successful revitalisation programme for the company.
